title: Restriction and extension by zero for modules on a localized site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $U$ be an object, and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topology and write $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal C)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal C/U)$ for the categories of sheaves of modules [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_U^*:\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal C/U)$ be restriction, $G\mapsto G|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and for a sheaf $F$ of $\mathcal O|_U$-modules let $j_{U!}F=P_F^\#$ be the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of its extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $P_F$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], functorial in $F$ (the *extension by zero*). Then $j_U^*$ is an exact functor, and $j_{U!}$ is an exact functor left adjoint to it: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(j_{U!}F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O|_U}(F,j_U^*G)$ naturally in the $\mathcal O|_U$-module $F$ and the $\mathcal O$-module $G$.

source.place: Section 03DH and Lemma 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero and exactness), with the same construction in sheaves of modules

proof.text: The restriction $j_U^*$ is a functor on module sheaves by the definition of the localized ringed site: it keeps the section groups and restriction maps on objects $V\to U$, and the action of $\mathcal O|_U(V\to U)=\mathcal O(V)$ is the restricted action. The extension-by-zero presheaf $P_F$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules by [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], and its module sheafification $P_F^\#$ is the stated $j_{U!}F$ by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Thus both assignments are functors on the displayed module categories.

source.place: Section 03DH and Lemma 03DI, construction of the module extension by zero

proof.text: Construct the module Hom equivalence directly, following the sectionwise formula of Stacks 03DI. From a map from the extension-by-zero presheaf to G, compose each section map with the direct-sum injection indexed by the slice arrow. Conversely, from F to the restriction of G, use DirectSum.toModule on the component linear maps. Naturality follows from the restriction formula of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and naturality in the slice. The direct-sum universal property proves both inverse laws; checking the same generators proves naturality in F and G. Compose this presheaf Hom equivalence with the module sheafification Hom equivalence of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (the interface in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]) and use Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. This produces the module adjunction without requiring a sectionwise formula from the abelian adjunction statement.

source.place: Lemma 03DI, adjunction construction, with the module linearity in the paragraph after the presheaf formula

proof.text: The module restriction is additive by its sectionwise formula in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Forget the short complex to abelian sheaves; exactness of the forgetful functor follows from [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Restriction commutes with forgetting by the identity natural isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact], transport the mapped short complex along this isomorphism, and use ShortExact.reflects_shortExact_of_faithful. The Mathlib characterizations of finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation for additive functors between abelian categories give both preservation clauses.

source.place: Lemma 03DJ, restriction exactness assertion and the module forgetful-functor lemma 03DA

proof.text: Compare extension-by-zero followed by forgetting with forgetting followed by the abelian direct-sum extension. The section objects are identical; equality of the maps follows by direct-sum induction, since DirectSum.lmap and DirectSum.toAddMonoid agree on every summand. Whisker this comparison with abelian sheafification and use the sheafification/forgetful isomorphism of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. The abelian adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint] and Mathlib's constructed sheafAdjunctionContinuous identify the abelian extension with the sheaf pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. This pullback is additive because it preserves coproducts and zero morphisms; transfer additivity along the comparison and reflect it through the faithful additive module forgetful functor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-exact] to the forgotten short complex, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to preserve its short exactness. Transport along the comparison of functors, reflect short exactness through the faithful forgetful functor, and apply the Mathlib finite-limit and finite-colimit characterizations as in Step 3.
